question: Which article of the Constitution provides for the State Legislative Assemblies?
solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Article 168**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 168** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the **constitution of Legislatures in States**. It mandates that for every state, there shall be a legislature consisting of the **Governor** and one or two houses. ***Hence, Article 168 is the correct answer.***
 
• It clarifies that in states where there are two houses, they are known as the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)** and the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)**. In states with only one house, it is the **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Article 170** specifically details the **composition of the Legislative Assemblies**. It stipulates that the Assembly should consist of members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies, with a maximum limit of **500** members and a minimum of **60** members. ***Hence, Article 170 is incorrect as it deals with composition rather than the provision for the house.***
 
• **Article 172** provides for the **duration of State Legislatures**. It states that every Legislative Assembly, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for **five years** from the date appointed for its first meeting. ***Hence, Article 172 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 174** deals with the **sessions of the State Legislature**, including **prorogation** and **dissolution**. It grants the **Governor** the power to summon the House and dissolve the Legislative Assembly. ***Hence, Article 174 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the State Legislature**: 
 
 
• The State Legislature is governed by **Part VI** of the Constitution, spanning from **Article 168 to 212**.
 
• Most Indian states have a **unicameral** system, meaning they only have a **Legislative Assembly**. 
 
• A **bicameral** system exists in only a few states where both a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Legislative Council** are present to ensure broader representation.
 
 
 
• **Membership Qualifications (Article 173)**:
 
 
• To be a member of the **Legislative Assembly**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and at least **25 years** of age.
 
• For the **Legislative Council**, the minimum age requirement is **30 years**.
 
 
 
• **The Legislative Council (Article 169)**:
 
 
• **Article 169** gives **Parliament** the power to **create or abolish** a Legislative Council in a state if the Legislative Assembly of that state passes a resolution by a **special majority**.
 
• Currently, only **six states** have a bicameral legislature: **Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Election**: Members of the **Legislative Assembly (MLAs)** are **directly elected** by the people on the basis of **adult suffrage**. In contrast, members of the **Legislative Council (MLCs)** are **indirectly elected** through a complex process involving local bodies, graduates, teachers, and nomination by the **Governor**.
 
• **Special Provisions for Small States**: While **Article 170** sets a minimum of **60** members for an Assembly, exceptions have been made for smaller states like **Sikkim (32)**, **Goa (40)**, and **Mizoram (40)** through various constitutional amendments to ensure administrative feasibility.
 
• **Officer of the House**: The **Legislative Assembly** is presided over by a **Speaker** and a **Deputy Speaker**, who are elected by the members of the Assembly from among themselves.
 
• **Role of the Governor**: The **Governor** is an integral part of the State Legislature (under **Article 168**) even though he is not a member of either House. No bill can become law without the **Governor's assent**.
